Summarize a co-occurrence network

Source: R/methods.R
summary.cooccurrence.Rd

summary() computes the metrics of a co-occurrence network at three levels: the network as a whole (size, density, mean degree, isolates and the distribution of edge weights and counts), each item in it (degree, strength and frequency), and, for a network built with split_by, each group. Together these show whether the network is sparse or saturated, which items are hubs, and how groups differ in size and density.

The metrics are returned as an object; printing it shows the network-level block. The node and group tables are returned as tidy data frames by as.data.frame.summary.cooccurrence(), or directly from the network with as.data.frame.cooccurrence().

For a network built with split_by, the frame stacks one network per group, so a pair can occur once per group. Pooled simple-graph metrics (density, mean_degree, possible_edges) are undefined and reported as NA; the node table has one row per node per group and the group table carries the per-group values. For the directed similarity = "relative" network, density is computed over ordered pairs and degree counts in- and out-edges.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'cooccurrence'
summary(object, ...)

Arguments

object

A cooccurrence edge list from cooccurrence().

...

Ignored.

Value

An object of class summary.cooccurrence: a list of network metrics (n_nodes, n_edges, possible_edges, density, mean_degree, isolates), the parameters used, five-number summaries of the weights and counts, a node table and, for split_by results, a group table. Read the tables with as.data.frame.summary.cooccurrence().

See also

print.summary.cooccurrence(); as.data.frame.cooccurrence(); plot.cooccurrence() for the degree distribution.

Examples

net <- cooccurrence(movies, field = "genres", sep = ",",
                    similarity = "jaccard")
summary(net)
#> cooccurrence network
#> ------------------------------
#> Nodes          : 22
#> Edges          : 129
#> Possible edges : 231
#> Density        : 0.5584
#> Mean degree    : 11.7273
#> Isolates       : 0
#> Transactions   : 1000
#> Similarity     : jaccard
#> Counting       : full
#> Weight range   : [0.001577, 0.2847]
#> Weight mean    : 0.04503
#> Count range    : [1, 159]
#> Count mean     : 13.23
#> Top nodes      : Drama(20, 1.178), Comedy(19, 0.9227), Action(17, 1.07), Romance(17, 0.5551), Adventure(15, 0.9235)

# The node table as a data frame
as.data.frame(summary(net), what = "nodes")
